Sports.title: End of the Worlds for the Rocket! Ronnie O'Sullivan's dream of title No 8 is dashed as he crashes out 13-12 to John Higgins in a Crucible epic
Sports.content:
Table-thumping Ronnie O’Sullivan saw his dreams of a history-making eighth World Championship shattered despite the best efforts of his celebrity pals.

UFC fighter Paddy Pimlett and Liverpool defender Milos Kerkez were at the Crucible roaring on the Rocket during his clash of snooker heavyweights with oldest rival John Higgins.

But it was Wizard of Wishaw Higgins, who had trailed 9-4, made three centuries in five frames en route to a memorable 13-12 second-round win — 30 years on from the prolific potting pair’s first Crucible meeting.

Frustrated O’Sullivan, who punched the table twice during the match, said: ‘If John plays like he did in the last session then he has a chance of winning the Championship.

‘I had my chance in the decider. I went into the pack, left myself a difficult red, I would have liked my hand on the table and then you never know, but I probably wasn’t the better player across the match anyway.

‘I felt all right. I’m enjoying my game, I feel like I’m in a much better place with my game this last month than I have been in the previous three years.

“A Crucible classic!” 😮



John Higgins wins the deciding frame against Ronnie O'Sullivan to reach the quarter-finals! pic.twitter.com/54kiFoa5Dp — TNT Sports (@tntsports) April 27, 2026

‘I just missed too many key balls, too many important balls which you can’t do.

‘This game is about playing well under pressure, there were some pressure times out there and I got tight. Maybe that’s because I haven’t won a tournament for about two and a half years.

‘I haven’t competed in any matches like that except against Neil [Robertson] in the final [of the Saudi Arabia Masters, which Robertson won 10-9].

‘It was a little bit of new territory for me again. I just have to be grateful for what I’ve got.’

Higgins punched the air in delight after completing a fine comeback.

The four-time world champion said: ‘I eventually came to the party. That was brilliant.

‘But listen, I thought Ronnie played in about the balls, that was the best I’ve ever seen him hit the ball. He was cueing it so well.

‘I thought [I had him] when I went 10-9 up. But the next two frames, the breaks that he made were incredible. It’s just incredible. You’re sitting there and you’re watching, and you’re admiring it, because you’re just saying, it’s incredible. But I was still feeling confident that if I get in, I could have a chance. And then I’ve hit him with two good frames.

Ronnie O'Sullivan exits the Crucible arena after his second-round defeat

...while it's joy for four-time champion Higgins, who reaches a 20th Crucible quarter-final

‘It’s only the second round. That’s the way I was looking at it. It’s a great match, but second round…this is how tough this tournament is.’

After resuming for the last session 9-7 up, O’Sullivan quickly saw his overnight lead evaporate as Higgins hit breaks of 59 and 118.

Higgins led for the first time in the match with a second successive century of 128.

The Rocket stopped the rot with a run of 63 and led 11-10 after a further visit of 93.

Higgins levelled once more with a third ton, this time 111, and moved 12-11 up with an 88.

O’Sullivan forced a fitting decider with a break of 81, but it was Higgins who held his nerve with a match-winning visit of 49.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes is the only choice for Footballer of the Year - but I'd give second place to a Spurs player, and here's why, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
It’s the 71st minute of Manchester United’s home game with Aston Villa last month. Michael Carrick’s side are drawing 1-1 with their rival for a Champions League spot. Casemiro plays the ball short to Bruno Fernandes, who is loitering near the touchline in front of the Sir Bobby Charlton Stand. Perhaps loitering is the wrong word. Fernandes is scanning. He’s alert to everything. He’s aware of everything going on around him on the pitch. He’s probably just about the most intelligent footballer in the Premier League. His mind works frighteningly fast. As Casemiro’s pass is rolling towards him, Fernandes sees Matheus Cunha start to make a run off the shoulder of Ezri Konsa, who is no slouch. Fernandes does not take a touch. He plays the pass first time, arrowing it inside Konsa. Konsa is beaten and the pass is so beautifully weighted that Cunha does not have to break stride. Cunha scores. Rinse that and repeat it. Over the course of this season, Fernandes has made 18 assists for his club, a mark that has even eclipsed David Beckham’s previous record for United set in 1999-2000. If Fernandes can create two more goals in United’s remaining five games, he will match the all-time Premier League record shared by Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne. No one else even comes close to him for the number of goals he has created for team-mates this season. Rayan Cherki, at Manchester City, and Jarrod Bowen, at West Ham, are next on 10. Fernandes has been wonderful to watch this season. Even when he was shackled by the deeper-lying position he was asked to occupy by Ruben Amorim earlier in the season, he was still a constant in terms of his quality and the example he set to his team-mates. He has been a beacon of class in a United season that has had many difficult moments. Fernandes has been wonderful to watch this season. He has been a beacon of class in a United season that has had many difficult moments Matheus Cunha thanks Fernandes for assisting his goal against Aston Villa. No one else comes close to Fernandes for the number of goals - 18 - he has created for team-mates this season

Your browser does not support iframes.

There have been times in the past when I felt the attitude of Fernandes towards referees, his constant complaining and his impassioned protesting, spoiled his talent in a United shirt and took away from his game. He was not my idea of what the captain of the side should be. But that has changed. This year, for many reasons, he has become a real leader in a team that desperately needed his leadership. And some of his football has been sublime. He is not a player in a team that is going to win the title but there is no one I have enjoyed watching more than him this season and that is why I am casting my vote for him as the Football Writers’ Association’s Footballer of the Year. There are plenty of other excellent candidates. Declan Rice has been outstanding at Arsenal, Bernardo Silva has been inspirational at Manchester City and Igor Thiago has been the season’s breakout star at Brentford. And if I could vote for a runner-up in the FWA poll, which will close next week, it would go to Archie Gray at Spurs, a young lad marooned in an awful team at a club in disarray. He is just about the only player at Tottenham whose reputation has been enhanced this season. Sometimes, it has seemed as if Gray has been asked to play in every outfield position in the Tottenham side and he has done it with class and style, dedication to a team ethic and an ability beyond his years. What a player he is becoming.

Your browser does not support iframes.

But Fernandes has been the season’s outstanding player. He has been United’s best player pretty much from the moment he joined the club from Sporting Lisbon in 2020. He has played through a time of upheaval at Old Trafford but his commitment to the team has not wavered. I admire that about him, too. There were rumours earlier this season that United wanted to cash in on him and sell him to Saudi Arabia but Fernandes has never agitated for a move anywhere, even though his talent deserved a better platform than the one United have been able to give him. Fernandes is the only United player who would get in any other team in the Premier League and yet he has always remained loyal to the club even when he must have despaired of the direction United were taking, as managers and interim managers and interim interims have come and gone. There is still some talk that United might want to sell him in the summer to finance a rebuild but that would be a horrible mistake from a club that has made a litany of horrible mistakes over the last decade or more. United should have learned by now that they need to build their team around Fernandes, not think about selling him. Michael Carrick, the caretaker manager, saw that straight away and acted on it. It helped to transform United’s season. It’s another reason why the club should make Carrick the permanent manager. Fernandes has been the best of United through one of the less successful eras of the club’s history. He has carried the team at times, taking the pressure of that on his shoulders. It is through him, as much as anyone, that the tide finally appears to be turning at Old Trafford. This year, for many reasons, Fernandes has become a real leader in a team that desperately needed his leadership Michael Carrick knew straight away that he needed to build the United team around Fernandes The last time a United player won the FWA award was in 2009-10 when it went to Wayne Rooney, and Rooney conducted a fascinating interview with Fernandes about his time with the club for the BBC last week. Fernandes talked about why he never considered moving away from United and why he wanted to create a lasting legacy for himself at the club by leading them to either the Premier League or the Champions League trophy. He identified his best moment in a United shirt so far as his assist for Kobbie Mainoo in the 2024 FA Cup final victory over Manchester City. It feels typical of him that he should have chosen a pass that created a goal for someone else to grab the headlines. McFarlane should not be blaming the media for Chelsea's plight Chelsea’s caretaker manager, Calum McFarlane, already appears to have developed an adversarial relationship with the media. When I asked him last week whether his shortfall in coaching badges might affect his authority over the players, he bristled. ‘What badges?’ he shot back. When I asked Calum McFarlane last week whether his shortfall in coaching badges might affect his authority over the players, he bristled. ‘What badges?’ he shot back If McFarlane really doesn’t know what badges he needs to coach in the Premier League, then he is even less experienced than we thought. Credit to him for getting a tune out of his team in the FA Cup semi-final against Leeds United at Wembley on Sunday. It was a fine achievement and he managed it with aplomb. But two things: if McFarlane is looking to blame someone for the demise of Liam Rosenior, he should be blaming the hierarchy at Chelsea, not the media. And even though it’s McFarlane on the touchline, we all know who’s in charge after the way Rosenior was disposed of. The players – and the army of five sporting directors – run the show at Chelsea.

Sports.title: Italy top-order star propels himself into frame to be England's new Test opener as rivals fail with the bat... and here's the selection shake-up designed to build bridges with the county game
Sports.content:
Italy top-order star propels himself into frame to be England's new Test opener as rivals fail with the bat... and here's the selection shake-up designed to build bridges with the county game

Emilio Gay is emerging as an outsider in the race to become England's new opening batsman with the favourites for the role failing to bash the door down in the County Championship.

Gay joined ex-Test players Haseeb Hameed and Dom Sibley in scoring a hundred in a round of bat-dominated fixtures that finished on Monday, outshining team-mate Ben McKinney in the process.

Although currently behind fellow left-hander McKinney and the bespectacled Asa Tribe, of Glamorgan, in the pecking order to replace Zak Crawley at the top of the order for England's Test series versus New Zealand in June, a man who currently plays international cricket for Italy - qualifying through his maternal grandfather - let his bat do the bidding once again.

The former Northamptonshire player crunched an unbeaten 159, his second three-figure score in three Division Two matches this summer, to help topple leaders Lancashire by eight wickets at Chester-le-Street.

On the day it was revealed that England's selection process has incorporated a recommendation from the post-Ashes review and is including a new layer of scrutiny from four leading county coaches, the 26-year-old took his season tally to 344 runs at a Bazballian strike rate of 74.

McKinney has a double hundred to his name, but little else in averaging 62.4 while Tribe massaged his figures for the summer with 67 unbeaten second-innings runs off a weary Leicestershire attack on a benign Cardiff surface to nudge his mark above 40 for 2026.

Emilio Gay could win an England Test call-up - despite playing international cricket for Italy

Gay, pictured on England Lions duty last November, qualifies for Italy through his maternal grandfather

Crawley began the 2026 campaign under intense pressure for his place after managing just five hundreds and averaging 31 in 64 Tests at the top of England's order, and has met the scrutiny with an underwhelming 118 runs in six innings for Kent.

Nottinghamshire captain Hameed struck 115 off 245 balls after Warwickshire enforced the follow-on at Trent Bridge and Sibley ground out 101 off 283 in another stalemate between Surrey and Essex at the Kia Oval.

However, despite vowing to give more credence to county returns when picking squads, they do not conform to the style to which England remain committed and are therefore unlikely to be considered viable partners for Ben Duckett, whose scores of 62 and 93 against Warwickshire ended a run of 12 first-class innings without a half century spanning back to last August.

While all four top-flight fixtures ended in draws, Gloucestershire emulated the positive results of Worcestershire and Durham in Division Two by defeating Derbyshire by 10 wickets at Derby.

The new four-man 'insight group' appointed to feed back on the best performers in county cricket comprises Derbyshire's Mickey Arthur, Anthony McGrath, of Yorkshire, Richard Dawson, who won promotion with Glamorgan last year, and Worcestershire's Alan Richardson.

They will meet with the ECB men's director Rob Key and England's other leading coaching personnel four times a year to provide feedback from the domestic game.

Their job will be to assess how those already on the radar of the ECB's scouting network are performing, effectively stress-testing the talent identification process with independent evaluation across the English season.

The introduction of the new panel comes after the winter review into England's failings in the Ashes concluded a disconnect had occurred with the county game when it came down to selecting squads.

Zak Crawley's place in the England XI is looking increasingly shaky due to his form for Kent

'He makes no contact with people, he doesn't want to talk about county cricket,' Sussex's Paul Farbrace said of England coach Brendon McCullum at the start of this season.

Indeed, McCullum will not arrive here from New Zealand until late next month and rarely watches the County Championship, fuelling the argument that England selection had become something of a closed shop, with the same players picked regardless of how they were performing.

It is expected that the four new sets of eyes will provide analysis on opposition players rather than their own, providing an inside track not only on the statistics they produce but how they have produced them.

Key will likely be at all of the quarterly meet-ups with Luke Wright's as yet to be named successor as national selector, performance director Ed Barney, head of player ID David Court and fast bowling lead coach Troy Cooley all joining on a rotational basis.

The first meeting is expected to take place ahead of the first Test against New Zealand on June 4.

This is a move designed to provide county form with greater heft when it comes to international honours, and directly addresses a requirement of the review for the England team to re-engage with the wider game.

Recently, the ECB have invested heavily in AI tools to aid the process of selecting England players, including the ground-breaking £500,000-a-year technology that sees each ball of domestic footage being captured by video cameras pinned to umpires.

It was thought that using this bank of data would help them earmark the individual characteristics required to create a photofit of a winning touring team in Australian conditions.

But the number-crunching lacked the emotional intelligence of experts and turning now to four highly-respected figures in the game will help on multiple levels.

Derbyshire coach Mickey Arthur (right) is part of England's new four-man 'insight group' appointed to feed back on the best performers in county cricket

In addition to providing expert input into things like a player's adaptability and reaction to external factors like pressure or fatigue, the insight group will help smooth relations between the England team and the pyramid it selects from.

Key simply cannot be across matches like a county coach and has chosen four legates - two from Division One, two from Division Two - with first-hand experience of the bridge from first-class cricket to the international stage.

In Arthur, he has arguably the most experienced active coach in the sport, one who has been in charge of four Test nations, comprising his native South Africa, Australia, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.



Meanwhile, Dawson has a working knowledge of the pathway system as part of the England set-up until McCullum thinned out the personnel when taking control of the white-ball teams 18 months ago, and both McGrath and Richardson have been seconded to work on tours in the past few years.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight deal is SIGNED: AJ announces his return to boxing after car crash that killed his friends - before he ends 10-year wait to fight Fury
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight deal is SIGNED: AJ announces his return to boxing after car crash that killed his friends - before he ends 10-year wait to fight Fury

The warm-up fight and the mega-fight to follow have both been signed by Anthony Joshua. Thereby ending a decade of speculation, argumentation, provocation and joculation between himself and Tyson Fury.

AJ will finally make his agonised comeback in Riyadh on July 25 against little-known, mostly-untested but allegedly big punching Albanian Kristian Prenga. That is part one of a deal which will come to a climax in the Battle of Britain with the Gypsy King.

So says Saudi paymaster Turki Alalshikh with this pronouncement on Joshua versus Fury: 'To my friends in Great Britain, it is happening, it's signed.'

The when and the where of it?

The date will be by the end of this year, most likely November. The place a little more likely Croke Park in Dublin than Wembley, which reinforces the certainty that this is all being made possible by loads of money.

To my friends in Great Britain - it’s happening 🦁. It’s signed ✍️🥊 — TURKI ALALSHIKH (@Turki_alalshikh) April 27, 2026

Tyson Fury (left) and Anthony Joshua have signed a contract to fight, claims Turki Alalshikh

Joshua will fight Kristian Prenga in his comeback fight first on July 25 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

When Joshua declared himself sufficiently recovered now from the psychological anguish of losing two of his best friends in that horrific December car crash in Africa he added: 'The landlord (as he calls himself) will collect his rent.'

As for Fury, who now resides in the tax haven of the Isle of Man, he would save millions by boxing AJ in the Emerald Isle rather than the UK.

And who could blame them? They have expended way more hours bringing this fight to reality than on their most recent fights. Namely AJ's circus act with YouTube celebrity Jake Paul in December and Fury's one-sided pummelling of Russia bear wrestler Arslanbek Makhmudov earlier this month.

After the latter Joshua, who was ringside in the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, declined tor respond to Fury's taunting. Now that both have negotiated their separate financial deals with His Excellency Alalshikh - potentially $20-30million each - the gloves are on.

Joshua says: 'It's no secret that I've taken some time to rebuild (following not only the loss of his friends but also his KO clobbering by Daniel Dubois) I'm ready to step back into the ring. I look forward to picking up where I left off.'

Fury says: 'Ours is the biggest fight in world boxing at the moment. In fact the only fight I've been interested in since I made my (fifth!) comeback.'

When Joshua and Fury do meet in the ring, Daily Mail Sport can exclusively reveal that Alalshikh is hopeful of having music superstar Dua Lipa in attendance and performing too. He is a big fan of the Brit's music and admires her rise to stardom.

Turki Alalshikh (left) is a big fan of British music superstar Dua Lipa and hopes she attends and performs at the Fury-Joshua fight

After beating Arslanbek Makhmudov earlier this month, Fury called out Joshua to fight him

Joshua survived a car crash at the end of last year which claimed the lives of his friends

As for the third man in this trilogy, Prenga has only one defeat on his record and has knocked out all his 20 victims. He says: 'Joshua is a great fighter but he has made a terrible miscalculation in picking me as his opponent.'



If so then Fury, who repeatedly warned Joshua not to risk an interim fight before they meet, will be infuriated.

Sports.title: 'It was a dangerous situation - and I was the guinea pig': OLLIE BEARMAN reveals how his horror Suzuka crash left him pleading with F1 bosses - and why he's 'ready' to replace Lewis Hamilton at Ferrari
Sports.content:
It seemed the natural first question to ask Ollie Bearman because the last time we saw him on a racetrack he was stumbling away from a 191mph smash at the Japanese Grand Prix in Suzuka.

‘How are you, Ollie, after the accident?’

‘Good, mate,’ he responded.

‘A big one that?’ I tried to suggest the notion with a grimace of sympathy on my face, a look of ‘yikes’.

‘You are starting with some great questions there,’ retorted Bearman, half-smiling, half-salty, his memories of the incident at the end of last month clearly still playing on his mind. ‘It’s not very nice, is it!’

There has been no chance for the Essex-born driver, a rising Formula One star aged 20 with realistic dreams of driving for Ferrari one day, to return to the track since the smash at Spoon Curve presented the only punctuation mark to his soaring early-season form. The incident occurred as he was trying to overtake Alpine’s Franco Colapinto, who made a defensive move that played its part in a 50G shunt that left Bearman with a bruised right leg.

‘You are starting with some great questions there,’ retorts Ollie Bearman to Daily Mail Sport, when reminded of his 191mph smash at Suzuka last month

The smash at Spoon Curve occurred as he was trying to overtake Alpine’s Franco Colapinto, with the 50G shunt leaving Bearman with a bruised right leg

Truly putting it behind him requires another race to act as balm, and hopefully revive his confidence fully. The opportunity to get straight back on the metaphorical bike was denied him because the war in the Middle East erased the Bahrain and Saudi Arabia editions that were due to take place this month.

He apologised to his Haas team for his part in the accident, knowing it would land them with a thousand-time bigger bill than that visited on your table for a congenial lunch at the Savoy, the London hotel of legend where we conduct this interview with a piano tinkling behind his left shoulder.

But the other part that mitigates his slight miscalculation was that this year’s new regulations introduced a huge speed differential as drivers build up their battery power. The split between old-school combustion engine and electric is too arcane to dwell upon here – a dangerous blight on F1, though the FIA have correctly introduced various modifications ahead of Sunday’s Miami Grand Prix to soothe the teething pains.

‘It’s not the end of the world but not a moment I was planning on,’ said Bearman of his prang. ‘For example, I was back home on Monday. I was on the simulator on Wednesday morning. It was just at the time when the adrenaline went down there was some pain in my leg, but it was short-lived. If the cancelled races had been on, I’d have been fine to drive.

‘The drivers have spoken to the FIA about these big speed deltas causing dangerous situations and I was a bit unhappy to be the guinea pig on that. The good thing is that the FIA are very receptive to our ideas and I am confident we will work everything out.’

We will get on to more glorious topics in a moment, but in a final word on the big accident, which has shaken the sport’s rule-makers as well as Bearman, he adds: ‘At the end of last year, a lot of us drivers were pushing our defensive moves to the absolute limit.

‘We were all close – eight-tenths covering us in qualifying and in the race. It was hard to pull off an overtaking move. The regs were mature – more than 10 years old with engines and more than five with the chassis.

‘Last year, Franco’s defence would have been on the absolute limit but with five-times the speed delta it was dangerous.’

Cycling fan Bearman has made the most of his downtime courtesy of cancelled races in the Middle East, attending the Paris-Roubaix to watch his friend Tadej Pogacar

His passion for cycling helps the 20-year-old offset his devotion to Percy Pigs

Well, moving on now, in a literal sense Bearman is back on his bike. Cycling is his self-declared favourite hobby, enjoyed in the French Riviera from his home in Monaco. ‘I love being in the mountains,’ he said.

‘I could spend hours up there.

‘I went to see my friend Tadej (Pogacar, the four-time winner of the Tour de France, with whom he rides) compete in the Paris-Roubaix.

‘It was the first cycling race I had been to. The Tour de France once started in my home town, Chelmsford, but I was too young to join my mum and dad who went to see it go down the high street. To see the peloton for the first time was so impressive.

‘I am a decent amateur cyclist. But when I compare myself to those guys, I am very, very slow.’

Nico Rosberg once gave up cycling so as not to add extra muscle weight around his knees and thighs in an all-out attempt to beat Lewis Hamilton, as he did successfully in 2016, and I wonder whether at 6ft 2in there is any danger in that for Bearman.

‘It is a trade-off,’ he reasoned. ‘You gain a bit of muscle but it also keeps the fat levels down so it works quite well. I have had to watch that over the last year as I’ve grown. But hopefully I won’t do any more growing… vertically.

‘The rules dictate that you have to be 82kilos with race suit and helmet when you are weighed. So that means being 79 kilos (12st 6lb) yourself. I have had to watch that over the break (he loves eating sweets, namely Percy Pigs and Colin the Caterpillar Fruit Sours from M&S), so that’s why I have been cycling!’

Haas are doing extremely well on limited resources, running the lowest budget on the grid, and lie fourth in the constructors’ championship

Essex-born Bearman is ultra-loyal to the team, but Ferrari is where he would like to end up

Haas are doing extremely well on limited resources, running the lowest budget on the grid, and lie fourth in the constructors’ championship with Bearman and his team-mate Esteban Ocon contributing points under the astute leadership of team principal Ayao Komatsu.

Bearman is ultra-loyal to the team, but Ferrari is where he would like to end up. It is where he started in F1, indeed, having been handed the seat for Jeddah in 2024 when Carlos Sainz went down with appendicitis. He had been brought into the Scuderia’s development programme three years earlier, so he is enmeshed in the Italian team.

Joining the Ferrari scheme entailed leaving home, his family, including his English Bull Terrier and Boston Terrier, to ask of the gods his destiny, a move to Maranello that leaves him with a non-Essex accent and one that is impossible to pin down, with its pan-European inflections. The relocation was a sign of his ambition, even having to fight off his mother Terri’s desire to see him finish his studies at King Edward VI Grammar School.

So, what about a full-time drive at Ferrari, if say Lewis Hamilton were to retire in the next year or two?

‘I feel like I am ready,’ he declared. ‘If I didn’t say that, it wouldn't be worth going to the track. I am young and have years to go. I just want to give them a reason for me to be a choice.

‘The faster I drive, the better my chances are.

‘I concentrate on myself, on giving my best performances for Haas. Just as the team debrief after every weekend, I do the same internally and with my coach as well. We make sure there is no stone left unturned.

‘I feel like I am ready,’ declares Bearman of his prospects of making the leap to Ferrari full-time. ‘If I didn’t say that, it wouldn't be worth going to the track'

‘It is not necessarily about the result you have achieved but about personal performance. You need to have no ego, no fear of criticising yourself. But you need a good level of self-confidence.

‘That allows you not to push blame elsewhere. For now, I am loving every minute of it.’

Bruised a few weeks ago, ‘The Bear’ is ready to fly again.

Now we're old and grey Fernando

Fernando Alonso, speaking at the Historic Grand Prix of Monaco, indicated he wants to carry on for another season.

At 44, and 25 years after he made his debut for Minardi, Aston Martin’s veteran Spaniard said: ‘For now, I am loving every minute of it.’

Some drivers never stop. Turning through the pages of history, the pre-War great Tazio Nuvolari never wanted to approach the final bend. Aged 55, he drove through Modena in the Mille Miglia of 1948. His bonnet was blown off, the car was lilting because of a broken spring, he had thrown out his seat and instead sat on a bag of oranges.

Enzo Ferrari watched this scene of defiance, turned away and wept.

Nuvolari remind you of anyone?

Aged 44, Fernando Alonso (left) is keen to race on. But so was a 55-year-old Tazio Nuvolari (pictured at the wheel) at the 1948 Mille Miglia, a sight that left Enzo Ferrari weeping

A Middle East revival? Don't be so sure...

Rumours surface that the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix may be reinserted into the calendar. I doubt this. The programme is packed and the summer heat in the Middle East precludes the race being staged during its hottest season.

The travelling troops are already exhausted by the interminable length of the modern calendar, now a ‘mere’ 22 races after the two omissions. So troubles there.

And that is before we get on to safety implications.

Another important sporting consideration is that the championship should not be distorted by the last-minute insertion of an extra race or two, offering a random 50 points as a potentially crucial moment in the season.

It would be like adding five minutes of fictitious stoppage-time to a football match. An undeserving winner might be scored in a final phoney minute.

Sports.title: Chelsea eye Premier League boss, whose team are above them in the table, in hunt for a new manager 'who is aligned with the club's vision' - with former Liverpool star also in the frame
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola is a candidate under consideration for Chelsea's managerial vacancy, according to sources, but pushing for the current Bournemouth boss could spark a head-to-head with Crystal Palace.

Iraola, the 43-year-old Spaniard who will leave his current club at the end of this season, is one of several names being reviewed by Chelsea's higher-ups after last week's sacking of Liam Rosenior.

However, Palace are believed to have spoken to Iraola's camp as they prepare for Oliver Glasner's own departure this summer, with sources adding they consider him their top choice.

Iraola is not the only name being studied by the Blues. Fulham boss Marco Silva is among the contenders as is former Liverpool midfielder Xabi Alonso, who was sacked by Real Madrid in January just six months after joining as head coach from Bayer Leverkusen. Both have experience in English football.

Chelsea intend to name Rosenior's successor once this season has ended. Sources have insisted they are taking a disciplined approach in identifying the right long-term appointment, adding they are targeting a head coach who is aligned with the club's vision, can develop their squad and deliver consistent performances and results.

Iraola, who will leave his current club at the end of this season, is one of several names being reviewed by Chelsea's higher-ups after last week's sacking of Liam Rosenior

Calum McFarlane, 38, will act as interim until that process is completed and started by leading Chelsea to a significant 1-0 win over Leeds on Sunday which set up an FA Cup final with Manchester City.

Enzo Fernandez scored the game's only goal while wearing the captain's armband in what was one of his more impressive performances.

Iraola has impressed while managing in the Premier League. Nearly three years after taking over Bournemouth, he now has them sitting in a European qualification position, and one point above McFarlane's Chelsea, who have a week to prepare for playing Nottingham Forest next Monday.

Palace will face Shakhtar Donetsk in their Conference League semi-final first leg this Thursday, then travel to take on Iraola's Bournemouth at the Vitality Stadium this weekend.

Sports.title: SIR CLIVE WOODWARD: Why sensational Noah Caluori must start for England against South Africa this summer - and what I see in him that I saw in Jonny Wilkinson 30 years ago
Sports.content:
As a coach, sometimes you see something in a young player which makes you stop and go: ‘Wow!’ It can be a piece of skill in training or a match or their demeanour which stands out. These are the moments you live for when you’re in charge of a team. I was fortunate to work with some incredible English talents, one of which was Jonny Wilkinson. I gave an 18-year-old Wilkinson his Test debut against Ireland in 1998. Was he ready to play internationally at that point? Probably not. But was it the right thing to do? Undoubtedly, yes. It is easy to say that now, given what Wilkinson went on to achieve. But even if he hadn’t become one of the best players England has ever seen, it still would have been the right call. In Wilkinson, I saw a young man not only with prodigious talent, but a calm, level-headed character. I saw no fear in Wilkinson and it was the same with Iain Balshaw and Mike Tindall – two more players I picked for England in their early years. Age should be no barrier to selection. Which brings me to Noah Caluori, the electric 19-year-old Saracens winger. There can be no doubt Caluori has been the breakthrough sensation of this season’s PREM Rugby, leading the way with 18 tries in just nine appearances. Ever since he was plucked from nowhere to make a try-scoring debut against Newcastle Red Bulls on the first weekend of the campaign, Caluori has stood out. Remarkably, he’s scored five tries in one game on two occasions – both against Sale. Last weekend, his acrobatic finish to score in Saracens’ win over Leicester saw him grab the headlines again. These are the sort of ‘wow’ moments I allude to and that you simply cannot ignore. I gave Jonny Wilkinson his England debut at just 18 in 1998 - I saw a player ready for the Test stage despite his tender years It's safe to say the decision paid off in the end, with Jonny going on to become one of the best players in England rugby history and us winning the World Cup together in 2003 Noah Caluori has been the breakthrough sensation of this season’s PREM Rugby, leading the way with 18 tries in just nine appearances I think it was sensible Caluori got a taste of the senior England setup last autumn and then played for the A team during the Six Nations. He has been handled well to date both by Mark McCall at Saracens and Steve Borthwick with England. But now is the time to give Caluori a first cap. I would bring him straight into the team for England’s next game – the blockbuster Nations Championship clash with South Africa in July. That statement is based on two points. The first is that Caluori clearly has the skills to excel in an England shirt. The second is that only by playing him can you find out what he can do at the highest level. If Borthwick – so long as he survives the RFU’s badly misguided post-Six Nations review into his position – thinks he’s ready, then I would urge him not to delay. Some people would say giving Caluori a Test debut against the double world champion Springboks in their own back yard would be brave, or even brainless. But as a coach, you have to be more pragmatic than that, looking at only the facts and not taking in too much emotion. England do have lots of good wingers. Immanuel Feyi-Waboso was a huge miss during the Six Nations, but he has been in superb form for Exeter since returning from injury and is a certain summer starter. Tommy Freeman is also on fire for Northampton, but as I’ve long maintained he should start at outside centre. That leaves a spot on the right wing, with Caluori facing competition from the likes of Tom Roebuck and Henry Arundell. Caluori has had a stronger season domestically than both of them. He has the ability to bring a real excitement to this England team alongside Feyi-Waboso, and that will be much-needed after the Six Nations which was more than disappointing. While Caluori is still very young and has lots of room to grow, he has all the attributes of a top-end wing. He is incredibly fast and, as he proved against Leicester, an exceptional finisher. Caluori is also exceptionally good in the air which is now, unfortunately, a big part of the game. Caluori’s defence has improved across the season too. I’ve seen the argument that England have nothing to lose against South Africa. For me, that’s not the case. The Springboks are formidable opposition, but they are beatable – even at home. If Australia can down Rassie Erasmus’ men in South Africa – as they did in last year’s Rugby Championship, stunning their hosts 38-22 having trailed 22-0 – then so too can England. Caluori has been the bane of Sale this season, scoring five tries in each of his two appearances against them As well as his superb finishing ability, Caluori is also exceptionally good in the air which is now, unfortunately, a big part of the game If Australia can storm South Africa's Ellis Park fortress, as they did last August, then it is definitely not beyond England

Your browser does not support iframes.

That Wallabies performance was full of attacking verve and can be a blueprint for England because with Feyi-Waboso, Caluori, Freeman and George Furbank in their team, England can certainly play the same way. Now that is a side I would have liked to coach! Borthwick is certainly under pressure after a Six Nations of just one win, but South Africa represents a chance for him to blow all that criticism away in the space of just 80 minutes. Caluori can be central to that plan. Lewis a shining example for England of today to follow I’d like to end my column by saying a big well done to the members of the current England team who attended a fundraiser for Lewis Moody in London last week. My interview with Lewis on his motor neurone disease diagnosis was a tough but important piece, raising awareness on the work being done to find a cure. Last Wednesday, I was at a gala dinner to support Lewis and the MND community. I was delighted to see Maro Itoje, Jamie George and Henry Pollock there too. The team of today can take inspiration from the successes of the past generation. For example, I couldn’t think of a better role model for Pollock to learn from than Lewis.

Sports.title: Galatasaray accuse Turkish Super Lig referees of having 'EVIL inside' them - despite beating bitter foes Fenerbahce
Sports.content:
Galatasaray accuse Turkish Super Lig referees of having 'EVIL inside' them - despite beating bitter foes Fenerbahce

Turkish giants Galatasaray have accused their country's top-flight officials of having 'evil inside' them in a scathing assessment on social media.

Galatasaray made the bold declaration on Sunday during their 3-0 win over bitter rivals Fenerbahce, who finished the match with 10 men, in the Istanbul derby.

In a top of the table clash, the victory moved Gala seven points clear of their foes with seven games remaining in the Turkish Super Lig.

But despite claiming victory, Galatasaray were left furious at the standard of officiating at their Rams Park.

While leading 1-0 at half-time, they wrote on X: 'Despite these referees, we're still leading 1-0.

'We see what you're doing, your plans, the evil inside you. Don't let the score distract you from the fact that TWO clear penalties for Galatasaray have been ignored by the referee and the VAR room in the first half.'

Don't let the score distract you from the fact that TWO clear penalties for Galatasaray have been ignored by the referee and the VAR room in the first half.#GSFB — Galatasaray EN (@Galatasaray) April 26, 2026

Galatasaray took to X on Sunday to accuse Turkish officials of having 'evil inside them'

Gala were unhappy with the perfomance of referee Yasin Kol during their win vs Fenerbahce

The in-game criticism came days after Galatasaray said it was suspending relations with the Turkish Football Federation in a dispute about picking referees for games.

Sunday's encounter saw referee Yasin Kol show a combined 11 yellow cards to both teams.

Gala, who are closing in on a fourth-straight Turkish title, took the lead in the 40th minute through Victor Osimhen - with Fener having earlier missed a penalty.

The hosts doubled their lead midway through the second half when Baris Alper Yilmaz scored a penalty.

Former Arsenal midfielder Lucas Torreira completed the scoreline on 83 minutes.

Fenerbahce goalkeeper Ederson, who joined from Manchester City last September, was sent off when the score was 1-0.

Complaints about referees and their integrity are common in the Turkish Super Lig.



Jose Mourinho, as Fenerbahce coach last season, was banned for four games by the federation for criticising match officials.

Sports.title: Beau Greaves breaks down in tears after historic PDC win as she says 'I can't believe it'
Sports.content:
Beau Greaves breaks down in tears after historic PDC win as she says 'I can't believe it'

Beau Greaves has become a trailblazer for all young female darts stars, but she broke new ground in an astonishing afternoon of darts for the prodigy

View 2 Images Beau Greaves struggled to hold back the emotions (Image: PDC Darts)

Beau Greaves became the first woman to win a PDC ranking title after beating three former world champions in a row. Greaves, 22, put together a monstrous run of form to claim Players Championship 11 in astonishing circumstances.

‌



The ProTour competition proved to be a history defining moment for women's darts in Milton Keynes. Greaves faced seven different opponents and beat them all, firstly edging out Aden Kirk and Thomas Lovely 6-4.

‌



She then overcame Jeffrey Sparidaans 6-2, before slightly getting the better of Czech star Karel Sedlacek. From then on, the pressure was cranked up to maximum temperature as she was pitted against 2018 World Champion Rob Cross.

‌



Greaves defeated Electric in a dramatic final decider, before being pitted against two-time Ally Pally King, Gary Anderson, in the final four. While many would have tipped the Flying Dutchman to get past 'Beau and Arrow' it was the 22-year-old who emerged as victor in dominant fashion.

She smashed Anderson 7-1, one year after he beat her in a dramatic final leg decider at the Grand Slam of Darts. After her ruthless triumph, she found herself one leg away from history.

Darts favourite Wayne Mardle finds new love 15 months on from wife's tragic death READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



The 2023 World Champion and former World No. 1 Michael Smith stood in her path. In another final leg decider, it appeared Bully Boy was going to take the title, after hitting 142 from 162 to leave a double ten finish.

Greaves was left on 142, but instead of buckling under the pressure, she lashed in two treble 20s and nailed double 11 to win the decider and become the first female winner of a PDC ranking title.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Interestingly, to Smith, it appeared to feel inevitable. When she hit the first treble, Bully Boy could be seen rolling his eyes, almost like he knew Greaves was going to checkout the 142.

When the second treble followed, he turned to his table and began putting his darts away, despite Greaves still needing to find the double 11. When she found the all-important match dart, she cheered, put both hands over her face and began to weep happy tears.

In their first to eight legs clash, she averaged 96.49, hit two 180s and checked out 80% of her attempts at a double, including a magnificent 170 finish, not long after she secured her triumph over Anderson with the Big Fish.

‌



View 2 Images Beau Greaves has shot into the top 100 over the last few weeks (Image: 2025 Getty Images)

Smith also showed his class by giving his younger opponent a huge and a pat on the back, while she tried to get to grips with her feelings of immense joy. After her victory was secured, an emotional Greaves said: "I’ve had a great year, but I never thought I’d win one of these. Never, ever.”

She added: “I can’t believe it. I was up a fair few legs and I started to think about it. It caught up with me.

‌



“I don’t know if I thought about being the first woman to do one. I can’t believe I hit that. I can’t believe I took out that.

“I have had a great year but I would never have thought I would win one. I had a good run last week and I said to the lads I sit on the table with that I felt like I hadn’t played well but I was getting results.

“Today I felt like I played really well. I am so happy I can’t even describe how I feel."

Sports.title: Mark Allen hit with 'sabotage' claims vs Barry Hawkins as duo face off at World Championship
Sports.content:
Mark Allen hit with 'sabotage' claims vs Barry Hawkins as duo face off at World Championship

Mark Allen and Barry Hawkins are set to face off once more

View 2 Images Mark Allen was his own worst enemy against Barry Hawkins in 2024 (Image: Alex Pantling, Getty Images)

The quarter-final stage of this year's World Snooker Championship has produced another meeting between Mark Allen and Barry Hawkins. The two have crossed paths before, most notably at the 2024 UK Championship, when Allen was accused of sabotaging his own chances.

‌



Allen saw off qualifier Zhang Anda in the first round at The Crucible this year before knocking out 2025 world champion Kyren Wilson with a 13-9 victory.

‌



Hawkins secured his second-round win with the same score-line against three-time champion Mark Williams, having defeated two-time World Championship runner-up Matthew Stevens to get his campaign underway.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

It has been just under 18 months since Allen and Hawkins last went head-to-head. Hawkins needed to come through qualifying in order to make the main draw, but beat top seed Ronnie O'Sullivan on his way to the semi-finals.

It was there that he encountered Allen, the fourth seed, with the Northern Irishman leading 4-2 and 5-4 but ultimately failing to close out the match. Snooker legend Steve Davis, working as part of the BBC's coverage, openly questioned whether Allen's slow play had led to his downfall.

‌



Ronnie O'Sullivan outburst as snooker star loses World Championship decider to John Higgins READ MORE :

Kyren Wilson lifts lid on wife's health battle after World Championship exit READ MORE :

Davis said: "It's tough sometimes playing this game and it does feel like both players are dragging each other down a bit. And it's just sometimes the balls go [Allen's] way.

"But question marks on whether Mark Allen [is] slightly sabotaging his own ability by playing a little bit slowly, and maybe Barry Hawkins [is] trying to get free and get a bit of rhythm going."

View 2 Images Hawkins took advantage to claim a narrow victory over Allen (Image: Getty)

‌



Hawkins emerged victorious, clinching a 6-5 win to secure his place in the final. However, he was no match for Judd Trump, with the third seed fending off a comeback to win 10-8.

Recalling his semi-final struggles, Allen admitted he was his own worst enemy. "I got what I deserved in the end," he said after losing out in York.

"I didn't take advantage of the chances I had, and I had quite a few. It's agonising because I got so close, despite playing poorly. Losing any Triple Crown semi-final is always hard to take but I think I've turned the corner this week. It's disappointing now, but there are plenty of positives."

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn breaks silence as Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight confirmed
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn breaks silence as Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight confirmed

After a future bout between Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury was recently confirmed, Matchroom chief Eddie Hearn took to social media and uploaded a post of his own

View 2 Images Eddie Hearn has issued a post on social media about Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury's upcoming clash (Image: YouTube/IFLTV)

Eddie Hearn has confirmed a bout between Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury is "signed, sealed, delivered." The bombshell news was confirmed this afternoon, not long after Joshua's next opponent was also revealed.

‌



The former World Champion and Olympic gold medallist will face Albanian boxer Kristian Prenga on July 25, before turning his attention to a clash against the Gypsy King later on in 2026. A date has not been confirmed for the bout between the two British titans, but it's expected to be in the final quarter of this year.

‌



It's a bout which has been more than ten years in the making, particularly after an undisputed world heavyweight clash between the pair was cancelled in 2021, after an arbitration judge ruled Fury should face Deontay Wilder in a trilogy bout, with the Bronze Bomber also rejecting a step-aside payment.

‌



Anthony Joshua takes dig at Tyson Fury with first words after agreeing fight READ MORE :

Joshua was also ordered to face Oleksandr Usyk in a mandatory WBO title defence, which ended with the Ukrainian outclassing him to win the title. Fury went on to beat Wilder, while Joshua faced Usyk in a rematch, only to lose again.

There were some negotiations for a bout in 2022, but the scenario became messy when Fury kept on imposing his own tight deadlines on a contract between the pair to be signed. This has not been the case this year, as Hearn confirmed on social media.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



The Matchroom chief uploaded a picture of himself, chairman of the Saudi Arabian General Entertainment Authority Turki Alalshikh and Joshua smiling, He wrote: "Signed, sealed, delivered! AJ v Fury is on!"

Joshua has already began the mind games with Fury, writing: "It’s no secret I’ve taken some time to consolidate and rebuild to be ready for stepping back into the ring and this is the next step on that journey. I’m looking forward to competing and picking up where I left off. As I said. The landlord will collect his rent. That is certain.”

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Fury is yet to comment specifically, but has has reposted an Instagram upload of Alalshikh confirming the news on X. However, considering the way he issued his challenge to Joshua immediately after he overcame Russian giant Arslanbek Makhmudov via an unanimous decision earlier this month, Fury will be feeling confident

After his victory, he turned to Joshua and shouted: "I want you, AJ, Anthony Joshua. Let's give the fight fans what they want - the Battle of Britain. I challenge you Anthony Joshua to fight me the Gypsy King next. Do you accept my challenge?"

View 2 Images Tyson Fury laid down the challenge to Anthony Joshua at the start of April (Image: 2026 Mark Robinson)

Article continues below

Of course, Joshua will have to overcome Prenga, the little known 35-year-old who has earned a reputation for being a strong knockout artist. He boasts a 20-1 record, with 20 coming via knockout.

His only loss came in February 2017, when he overcame Giovanni Auriemma in the Netherlands. Hearn had frequently said Joshua was going to have a 'warm-up' fight before any clash with Fury, having most recently fought Jake Paul in a lucrative bout, before surviving a horrific car crash in Nigeria, which claimed the lives of his friends Sina Ghami and Latif Ayodele.

Sports.title: Rory McIlroy has passed up on £13.7m after snubbing Donald Trump in latest announcement
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy has passed up on £13.7m after snubbing Donald Trump in latest announcement

Donald Trump was looking forward to watching Rory McIlroy play at Trump National Doral during the Cadillac Championship, but the back-to-back Masters champion is sitting out the PGA Tour signature event

View Image Trump National Doral will not see Rory McIlroy play there in the Cadillac Championship (Image: Getty Images)

Rory McIlroy has now withdrawn from five PGA Tour signature events since the start of last year after skipping this week's Cadillac Championship. Donald Trump spoke after his second Masters win about looking forward to watching the Green Jacket holder play at Trump National Doral.

‌



McIlroy, 36, will not be in Miami, though, foregoing a chance to play for the £2.7million top prize. He has now missed consecutive signature events after skipping The Heritage.

‌



That tournament took place just a week after his latest win at Augusta National. McIlroy also missed it last year after completing the career Grand Slam.

‌



Ryder Cup organisers issue ticket price statement after backlash to 'extortionate' hike READ MORE :

The Heritage winner, Matt Fitzpatrick, took home £2.7m, bringing the total that his Ryder Cup teammate has passed up in April alone to £5.4m. McIlroy also missed the Memorial Tournament last year for the first time since 2017.

Winning the event Jack Nicklaus hosts earns players £2.9m, with Scottie Scheffler topping the leaderboard the last two years - McIlroy has never. The other signature event he missed last year was the Sentry, in what proved to be its last edition before being cancelled in 2025.

Hideki Matsuyama won the £2.7m prize that McIlroy forewent. That takes the total of potential signature-event winnings he decided against competing for to £13.7m.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

His absences have not gone unnoticed on the Tour either. Michael Kim said on Friday: "I hope to get to a point where I decide to skip a signature event even when healthy."

That post on X seemed to reference the Masters champion missing another one, though Kim later said it was OK in another post. He made the follow-up in response to GOLF.com. writer Sean Zak describing McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler missing three signature events between the Masters and PGA Championship as "one problem the PGA Tour needs to solve".

‌



Kim said on the social media platform: "It's OK. Scottie is just skipping Truist to play the two DFW events." Kim appears to cite Scheffler's participation in two Dallas-Fort Worth events as the reason for missing the upcoming Truist Championship, which McIlroy is due to play.

He said in January: "I think I need to show up at tournaments with enthusiasm every single time, so, playing in the places that I want to play, playing the tournaments I want to play, not feeling like I’m at a tournament because I’m obligated or have to be there, but because I want to be there."

Sports.title: Chelsea next manager: Xabi Alonso added to shortlist as opening contact made
Sports.content:
Chelsea next manager: Xabi Alonso added to shortlist as opening contact made

After sacking Liam Rosenior and appointing Calum McFarlane on an interim basis, Chelsea are searching for their next permanent manager, and three names on their shortlist have emerged

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso is on Chelsea's shortlist (Image: Ricardo Larreina/Europa Press via Getty Images)

Chelsea will make checks on both Xabi Alonso and Marco Silva after contacting Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola in their search for a new manager. The Blues sacked Liam Rosenior last week on the back of suffering five consecutive Premier League defeats, leaving their Champions League hopes in tatters.

‌



Calum McFarlane will take charge of first-team duties until the end of this season after guiding Chelsea to the FA Cup final with Sunday's 1-0 victory over Leeds. McFarlane will then be a replaced by a permanent successor to Rosenior, who lasted just three months in the Stamford Bridge hot seat.

‌



It emerged on Monday that Chelsea have made contact with Iraola, 43, who's already confirmed to be leaving Bournemouth upon the expiry of his contract in June. But the Spaniard isn't the only manager under consideration, the Telegraph report.

‌



Fulham boss Silva, who like Iraola is out of contract this summer, is also set to be contacted. As is Alonso, who was sacked by Real Madrid in January after just seven months in charge, and the former Liverpool midfielder is under the same representation as compatriot Iraola.

WORLD CUP LEGENDS: The stars who lit up football's greatest tournament - Buy the Special Edition today

Trevoh Chalobah hits back at Chelsea critics after response to Liam Rosenior accusations READ MORE :

Those three aren't the only coaches on Chelsea's shortlist, though, with other unnamed candidates also being discussed. Their group of five sporting directors will spearhead the process of appointing the club's sixth permanent manager since Chelsea were purchased by Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital's consortium in 2022.

‌



The Blues have a week until they play again, hosting relegation-threatened Nottingham Forest next Monday afternoon. While Alonso and Iraola are both available for hire in the summer as things stand, Silva's future at Fulham remains undecided.

Who should Chelsea appoint as their next manager? Let us know your pick in the comments section.

View 2 Images Chelsea plan to speak to Marco Silva's camp, having already contacted that of Andoni Iraola (Image: GLYN KIRK/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



When asked last week if there'd been any progress regarding his future, the Portuguese snapped: "No. Why is it different this week? It is not at all.

"It is the same and the same answer that I said to you already last week, it is the same. I will not make, every single week, comments about [my future].

"When something comes new, we are going to tell from ourselves, myself and the club. Everything what I need, or the club needs to do with me is going to be between me and the club."

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham's reason for snubbing Man Utd transfer despite private tour of Old Trafford
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham's reason for snubbing Man Utd transfer despite private tour of Old Trafford

Manchester United fell short in their efforts to tempt Jude Bellingham to Old Trafford despite a private tour of the club and the promise of early riches

View 2 Images Jude Bellingham rejected the chance to join Manchester United six years ago despite the club's committed attempts (Image: CRISTINA QUICLER, AFP via Getty Images)

Virtually every major European giant was vying for the signature of Jude Bellingham in the summer of 2020. Manchester United were no exception and extended an invitation to the Birmingham City wonderkid to visit their Carrington training ground in a bid to win him over.

‌



Bellingham was still only 16 when he was shown around what could have become his new home alongside his parents in March 2020. The trip included a meeting with Old Trafford legend Sir Alex Ferguson, while former chief executive Ed Woodward was understood to have played a significant role in orchestrating the visit.

‌



As it transpired, the now-22-year-old snubbed the advances of several heavyweights, including United and Chelsea, opting instead to join Borussia Dortmund. It's fair to say the decision has paid dividends for the England star, who spent three years in Germany before completing a move to Real Madrid in a deal potentially rising to £113million.

‌



Sky Sports reported at the time that Bellingham had been impressed by what he witnessed at Carrington. This is despite the training facilities having undergone a significant overhaul since Sir Jim Ratcliffe assumed control of the club's day-to-day operations.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

As for why he rejected United, it was reported Bellingham's parents, Denise and Mark, believed his development would be better served in the Bundesliga. Dortmund highlighted Jadon Sancho as proof of how rapidly young players can flourish in Germany following his rapid rise after departing Manchester City.

‌



Jude Bellingham buys stake in cricket team as Real Madrid star joins The Hundred READ MORE :

Top five salaries in Premier League and La Liga compared with Erling Haaland only third READ MORE :

It seems the Bellingham family concurred, demonstrated by the fact Jude's younger brother, Jobe, also now represents the Black and Yellows. The elder sibling was indeed handed immediate opportunities to shine in front of the Yellow Wall, chances he may not have been afforded had he moved to Old Trafford.

Former Birmingham City CEO Xuandong Ren told Mundo Deportivo Bellingham declined a substantially higher wage when he rejected United and others. That was one of the earliest indicators regarding Bellingham's determination to chart the course he imagined.

"Jude did not make any decision based on money," said Ren in 2022. "They were offering much more salary compared to the rest. Maybe double. He was going to be guaranteed millions in the bank and he didn't take it. That's not normal for a player at all."

‌



View 2 Images Bellingham was arguably the most in-demand prospect on the planet when he left Birmingham in 2020 (Image: Catherine Ivill/Getty Images)

That story once more illustrates the player's dedication to being the architect of his own future. And it suggests United were perhaps waging a losing battle to attract the midfielder at that point in his career.

Bellingham and Sancho were team-mates at Dortmund for one season before the latter made the switch to Old Trafford. However, by the time Bellingham's signature came back on the market in 2023, Sancho found himself firmly out in the cold at United.

‌

That decline in fortunes may have influenced Bellingham's decision not to follow his friend's path. Then again, it's equally possible the allure of the Bernabeu just proved too strong to resist and United were once more left trailing in the pecking order.

Bellingham, whose Real contract runs until 2029, hasn't sparkled this season quite like he did during his opening two Spanish campaigns. However, having battled through several injury problems this term, Birmingham's former prodigy will get his opportunity for redemption when England head to World Cup 2026 this summer.

Sports.title: Four men charged after incident at Rochdale vs York City title decider
Sports.content:
Four men charged after incident at Rochdale vs York City title decider

Four men have been charged over a reported incident after York City scored a dramatic equaliser to win the National League title

View 2 Images York City celebrate the team's promotion and title victory with the trophy following their draw against Rochdale (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Four men have been charged in connection with an incident which was reported at the end of the Rochdale AFC v York City match on Saturday, April 25. Police were called following the game between both sides at the weekend.

‌



Greater Manchester Police have confirmed on Monday that four men will appear before magistrates later this year following the alleged incident. Kiean Sultan, 18, of Thirlmere Drive, Middleton, has been charged with pitch encroachment and Section 4 of the Public Order Act.

‌



Aaron Dawson, 31, of Smithies Street, Heywood, has been charged with two counts of Section 4B of the Public Order Act. Sam Manicolo, 18, of Hollins Drive, Middleton, has been charged with pitch encroachment. Thomas Coleman, 23, of Blenheim Street, Rochdale, has been charged with pitch encroachment.

‌



Rochdale vs York ends in dramatic scenes after pitch invasions and controversial goal READ MORE :

One man was initially arrested at the scene but later de-arrested. All four men have been bailed and are due to appear at Manchester and Salford Magistrates on August 18.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Saturday's match saw York score an incredible 103rd-minute equaliser to win the National League title. The Minstermen had one hand on the trophy heading into stoppage time at the Crown Oil Arena with a draw enough to seal promotion.

‌



Yet with time running out, the match descended into pandemonium. Mani Dieseruvwe netted a superb header in the 96th minute for Rochdale, triggering jubilant scenes and a pitch invasion. A victory for Dale would see them promoted as champions, and they believed they'd found a crucial goal.

View 2 Images York City sealed promotiom with their dramatic draw against Rochdale (Image: Getty Images)

Veteran forward Ian Henderson came off the bench to deliver a moment of brilliance. The 40-year-old curled the ball into the far post with the outside of his foot, and Dieseruvwe rose highest to power a header past York City shot stopper Harrison Male.

‌



Rochdale fans flooded onto the pitch to celebrate what they assumed would be the title. Following a five-minute delay, supporters were cleared from the pitch and play continued.

York then pushed players forward and scored an astonishing equaliser in the 103rd minute through Josh Stones, to clinch the title in sensational fashion.

Callum Howe's header was cleared off the line before the ball fell to Stones at the far post. He forced the ball towards the goal, though there were doubts over whether it had actually crossed the line, with York players insistent they'd secured the winner.

Article continues below

The officials awarded the goal, and the travelling away fans surged onto the pitch. It lead to absolute bedlam as York players, staff and supporters celebrated frantically on the sidelines.

Sports.title: Arsenal target Julian Alvarez wanted by rival club as transfer approach emerges
Sports.content:
Arsenal target Julian Alvarez wanted by rival club as transfer approach emerges

Julian Alvarez has been regularly linked with a return to the Premier League since leaving Manchester City and the Atletico Madrid star is once again attracting transfer interest

View 2 Images Barcelona are set to try and sign Julian Alvarez (Image: Europa Press via Getty Images)

Barcelona are said to have made contact with their domestic rivals Atletico Madrid over an ambitious deal for Julian Alvarez with the club set to prioritise signing a new No 9 this summer.

‌



Arsenal are known to be among Alvarez's many suitors, although Atletico are in a strong bargaining position given the 26-year-old is under contract until 2030. The striker's teams include a release clause set at a staggering €500m (£432.9m) - but that hasn't deterred interest from the reigning Spanish champions.

‌



Barcelona head coach, Hansi Flick, is understood to have asked the club hierarchy for a new striker this summer and Alvarez is the man the La Liga giants want to team up alongside Raphinha and Lamine Yamal next season.

‌



ESPN claim Barcelona have already made contact with Atletico in order to discover the club's stance on selling the player they signed from Manchester City back in 2024.

Arsenal set for financial boost as Ethan Nwaneri's Marseille nightmare worsens READ MORE :

Is Pep Guardiola about to quit Man City? The hints which suggest he might say goodbye READ MORE :

Though any prospective deal would fall some way short of the extraordinary figures in Alvarez's release clause, Barcelona would be willing to close a deal worth €95m (£82.2m) inclusive of add-ons. Atletico, on the other hand, are willing to counteract any proposals by offering Alvarez a lucrative new contract until 2032 to keep him at the club.

Barcelona have been plagued by financial difficulties in recent years and are currently operating just outside of La Liga's financial fair play rules, meaning there are limits on what they can spend.

‌



However, the club 'hope to move within the league's regulations' this summer, which would potentially help facilitate larger spends, while Alvarez's willingness to transfer could also aid any potential deal.

View 2 Images Alvarez is a wanted man with Arsenal among his many admirers (Image: Getty)

Barca are long-term admirers of Alvarez, who they scouted back in his River Plate days. The attacker is even viewed as the perfect long-term successor to Robert Lewandowski, who turns 38 later this year.

‌



Arsenal's interest in Alvarez emerged back in January and they too could court the Argentine in the summer in a bid to boost their firepower.

The Gunners signed Viktor Gyokeres for a significant fee from Sporting Lisbon back in the summer but Kai Havertz was selected ahead of him in the pivotal meeting with title rivals Manchester City earlier this month, while there has been plenty of scrutiny over the Swede's tally of 12 goals in 32 Premier League games as well as his all-round performances.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
